title: Operator Miniapps: Autonote + Playlet Regenerator for Guided Remediations
creator: Leah Kim
description: Build a small-suite of operator-facing miniapps that convert curated runbooks into guided, parameterized workflows. Two primary components: (1) Autonote — automatic incident note generation and step suggestion engine that pre-populates runbook inputs from signals and past executions; (2) Playlet Regenerator — tool that synthesizes past manual remediation sequences into reusable, parameterized 'playlets' (templated micro-runbooks) with provenance and safety metadata. Goal: reduce toil, shorten MTTR, and create high-quality artifacts for later templating/automation.
acceptance_criteria: Autonote generates incident draft with at least 3 suggested runbook steps populated with inferred parameters from telemetry for >70% of test incidents
Playlet Regenerator converts an annotated incident log into a reusable playlet with input schema, dry-run simulation, and audit metadata
Operator miniapp UX flows include an explicit safety confirmation and the ability to run in dry-run/preview mode
All executions produce audit tags and attach to incident timeline; Telemetry dashboard shows run rates and failure modes
PRs merged with unit/integration tests; feature behind feature flag for initial rollout
comments: 2025-02-13 — Kickoff: scoped MVP to two high-value runbooks (redis-restart, cache-warmup). Decision: target hosted + dedicated control plane first, defer on-prem packaging to a follow-up.

2025-02-18 — Design sync: UX wants a two-column guided flow (left: suggested steps, right: parameter inspector). Trade-off: fewer configurable knobs to keep cognitive load low vs. power-user mode later. Agreed to implement compact advanced panel for power users.

2025-02-20 — Engineering note: implemented initial Autonote inference using heuristic rules over 'ops.telemetry.error_rate' and runbook invocation history. Accuracy fine-tuning required; created small labeled dataset from past 120 incidents.

2025-02-25 — Security review request submitted. Early feedback: require action whitelisting for privileged steps, and ensure KMS-backed consent logs. Added security_review_required flag and dependency on ENG-168401 for KMS integration.

2025-02-27 — PR feedback (github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1427): runtime safety checks should run server-side with debounce to avoid duplicate remediations. Marco to update PR with idempotency token support.

2025-02-28 — QA: dry-run mode validated for redis-restart; false-positive parameter inference noted in 2/10 cases where cluster name ambiguous. Created follow-up ticket ENG-160999 to improve entity resolution heuristics.

2025-03-01 — PM review: propose rollout plan to internal SRE squad as canary for 2 weeks; will gate on zero-sev incidents and operator feedback score >= 4/5. Added release flag 'console-2025.04-canary'.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus review on: 1) audit trail completeness and KMS tagging; 2) dry-run fidelity for playlets; 3) UX clarity around irreversible steps. Also verify that the operator consent modal records a unique consent token and attaches it to the incident timeline.
next_steps: Finish server-side idempotency token implementation and update PR
Integrate KMS tagging flow with consent modal (dependency ENG-168401)
Expand labeled dataset for Autonote entity resolution to 500 incidents
Run internal SRE canary and collect operator feedback using short pulse survey
